items.summary: Blind quantum computing (BQC) allows a client with limited quantum capabilities to delegate quantum computations to a more powerful server while hiding the computation. We introduce a four-state unit-disk crossing cell that couples directly to adjacent cells, with interfaces enforcing one-sided propagation: along occupied paths directed away from the diagonal, copy bits are nondecreasing.

items.title: Rugosity as a measurement-induced relative entropy
items.summary: Quantum-state rugosity quantifies the departure of a quantum state from the flat superposition associated with a prescribed basis. We show that rugosity equals the classical relative entropy generated by the binary flat-state measurement.

items.title: The integrable Lie-Trotter-Suzuki decomposition for nonlinear dynamics: Efficient Hamiltonian simulation of the Stepanoff flow
items.summary: We propose an efficient unitary numerical time integration strategy for nonlinear dynamical systems: the integrable Lie-Trotter-Suzuki decomposition (I-LTS). First, express the generator as a sum of integrable parts.

items.title: Sharp Transitions of Copy Complexity in Local Certification of Typical Pure States
items.summary: We determine the asymptotic copy complexity of $n$-qudit state certification with tensor-product measurements. For given acceptance and rejection fidelities $a$ and $b$ ($b<a$), the optimal copy complexity is $Θ(n^r)$.

items.title: Unitary Synthesis with a Unary Tracker
items.summary: This manuscript studies general unitary synthesis using unary-encoded ancillary register. Our first construction focuses on the $T$-cost of unitary synthesis. We maintain a unary register that coherently tracks the computational-basis label of the data.

items.title: Rényi multi-entropy from Riemann surfaces
items.summary: We compute vacuum tripartite Rényi multi-entropy in a two-dimensional compact-boson conformal field theory (CFT). For every integer Rényi index $n\geq2$, we evaluate the partition function on the replica Riemann surface for disjoint intervals, obtaining the twist four-point function in terms of a ratio of theta functions.

items.title: Slow mixing of Gibbs sampling for the quantum Curie-Weiss model
items.summary: Hamiltonian evolution can spread local operators across a dense quantum magnet. We show that this global support does not remove the bottleneck to thermalization in the quantum Curie-Weiss model: at fixed low temperature and weak transverse field, the Chen-Kastoryano-Gilyen Gibbs sampler [arXiv: 2311.09207] has an exponentially large mixing-time lower bound.

items.title: Magic Moments: An Operational Approach of Certifying Nonstabilizerness from Few Copies
items.summary: Magic is the key resource enabling universal fault-tolerant quantum computation beyond classically simulable stabilizer circuits. Certifying it, however, usually requires either full state tomography or an optimization over the set of stabilizer states, both of which rapidly become prohibitive as the system grows.

items.title: The asymptotic spectrum of tensors is connected
items.summary: We prove path-connectedness of the asymptotic spectrum of complex tensors of every fixed order $k \geq 3$: every spectral point is connected by a path to every "one leg versus the rest" flattening rank. In particular, the asymptotic spectrum evaluated at any fixed tensor is a closed interval, answering a question of Strassen.

items.title: Why do single photons produce interference fringes? The phase of a mode and the phase of a state
items.summary: If the phase of a photon-number state is completely undetermined, how can single photons, sent one at a time through a two-slit apparatus, build up interference fringes? These lecture notes answer this question from first principles.

items.title: Dynamics of a Charged Particle on a Conformal Helicoidal Surface
items.summary: We study the classical and quantum motion of a charged particle on a conformal helicoidal surface embedded in four-dimensional Euclidean space. A uniform ambient magnetic field pulls back to a nonuniform surface field.

items.title: Resource theory of pi-ordered imaginarity and its resource quantifiers
items.summary: Conventional resource theory of quantum imaginarity takes real density matrices as free states without ordering constraints on their diagonal populations. Motivated by the role of population ordering in the incoherent ergotropy of quantum batteries and the recently proposed framework of $π$-ordered coherence, we develop the resource theory of $π$-ordered imaginarity.

items.title: High-Throughput GPU Decoding of Quantum Bivariate Bicycle Codes under Circuit-Level Noise
items.summary: Bivariate bicycle (BB) codes reduce the physical-qubit overhead of quantum error correction compared to other codes such as Surface codes, but circuit-level faults create dependencies across measurement rounds that limit decoding throughput. We present a parallel-window GPU decoder that combines reusable fault patterns, compact shared-memory state, and persistent GPU workers using min-sum with Relay-BP recovery.

items.title: Noise threshold for learning with quantum memory
items.summary: A quantum memory can reduce exponentially the number of experiments needed to learn a physical process, but real memories are noisy. Here we show that, for Pauli memory noise with eigenvalues $λ_X,λ_Y,λ_Z$, the advantage is governed by $λ_X^2+λ_Y^2+λ_Z^2$.

items.title: Exponential Analysis for Trace-Distance Errors in Quantum Information Theory
items.summary: We study the trace-distance error in classical-quantum soft covering, privacy amplification against quantum side information, convex splitting, and decoupling by a Haar-random unitary followed by partial trace. In the independent and identically distributed setting, we determine exact reliability functions and strong converse exponents for soft covering with independent codewords, uniform convex splitting, and Haar partial-trace decoupling.

items.title: Quantum dynamics of a charged particle on rotating curved surfaces and space curves in electromagnetic fields
items.summary: We develop a gauge-consistent framework for a charged particle confined to a rotating curved manifold in an electromagnetic field, starting from the covariant Klein--Gordon equation. The non-relativistic reduction casts the rotational effects as effective gauge potentials while preserving the $U(1)$ symmetry, so that rotation and the external field enter alike, the geometry entering separately as the da Costa potential.

items.title: Experimental characterisation of compilation-dependent Grover--Rudolph probability distribution loading on a three-qubit NMR processor
items.summary: Exact state-preparation circuits are normally judged by how closely the measured output distribution reproduces the target. Using the ancilla-free Grover-Rudolph construction compiled into {Ry, X, CNOT}, we ask instead how much the accuracy of a probability-distribution loading depends on which of several logically equivalent compilations is executed.

items.title: Planckian bounds on thermalization times of strongly coupled open quantum systems
items.summary: We consider whether the thermalization of strongly coupled open quantum systems, whose equilibrium state is the mean-force Gibbs (MFG) state, is constrained by a fundamental Planckian time scale, $\hbar/k_B T$. By requiring that the same process thermalizes a family of nearby system Hamiltonians, we obtain a lower bound on the thermalization time, irrespective of the specific system-bath dynamics.

items.title: Intrinsically nonlinear nanomechanical resonator toward the single-phonon Kerr regime
items.summary: Manipulating a physical system at the single-quantum level typically requires an anharmonic energy spectrum. Nanomechanical resonators, however, are commonly admitted to be linear objects in the single-phonon regime, thus motivating most efforts to employ external sources of nonlinearity at the cost of added relaxation and decoherence channels.

items.title: Squeezing-preserving coherent control in Fourier-shaped optical lattices
items.summary: Motional squeezed states of atoms in optical lattices are affected by the anharmonicity of the trapping potential. Unequal vibrational energy spacings cause dephasing among the occupied motional-state coherences, leading to distortion of the wavepacket and a reduction in squeezing.

items.title: On the performance of nanoscale detection methods in NV-center spectroscopy
items.summary: Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) in subfemtoliter volumes operates in a regime where statistical fluctuations of the nuclear magnetization can exceed its thermal mean. Solid-state quantum sensors such as nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond are sensitive enough to detect NMR signals from such small volumes, which has motivated several detection protocols, based either on correlating the statistical polarization or on coherently detecting hyperpolarized samples.

items.title: The transverse spin-gradient approximation in noncollinear spin density functional theory
items.summary: We prove a quantitative error bound for a fixed-axis variant of the transverse spin-gradient approximation (TSGA) in noncollinear spin density functional theory. Inspired by Eich and Gross, we use a spin-spiral wave (SSW) as the local reference for the grand-canonical Levy-Lieb energy with the Hartree term subtracted.

items.title: Search-for-Gradient: Search-Based Restarts for Optimisation in Structured Flat Landscapes of Variational Quantum Algorithms
items.summary: Variational Quantum Algorithms (VQAs) are a promising class of hybrid quantum-classical algorithms that involve parameterised quantum circuits and classical optimisation. VQAs have found applications in simulation, optimisation, and machine learning.

items.title: Quantum Algorithm for Direct Estimation of Energy-Level Differences via Quantum Dynamics Simulation
items.summary: We present a quantum algorithm for the early fault-tolerant quantum computing (early-FTQC) era that estimates minute energy-level differences, such as energy gradients and molecular forces, at a lower sampling cost than existing phase-estimation methods. Such energy derivatives, accessed as the small energy difference induced by an infinitesimal parameter shift, are central to quantum simulation in chemistry and materials science.

items.title: Ancilla-Assisted Accelerated Readout of Transmon Qubits
items.summary: We present a scheme for accelerating dispersive readout of superconducting transmon qubits. Dispersive readout works by weakly coupling the target transmon to a resonator, such that the resonator experiences a state-dependent frequency shift, which can then be read out.

items.title: Geometry, masking and selection in Differential Evolution and SOMA on quantum state manifolds
items.summary: Differential Evolution (DE) and the Self-Organizing Migrating Algorithm (SOMA) generate new candidates through vector arithmetic: they subtract population members, scale the difference, and mask coordinates. Many practical search spaces are not vector spaces, however.

items.title: Scaling laws for quantum reflection of hydrogen isotopes on silicon
items.summary: Quantum reflection is a counter-intuitive process occurring when an atom is reflected by a rapidly-varying attraction towards a surface, for example the Casimir-Polder force. The reflection probability depends on the attractive potential and on the mass of the atom.

items.title: Beyond-quantum correlations for single system in pseudo-quantum model
items.summary: Within the standard prepare-measure framework, it has been demonstrated that certain compositions of two elementary quantum systems can produce beyond-quantum correlations and can even lead to perfect discrimination of two non-orthogonal quantum states. In this Letter, we introduce the pseudo-quantum model (PQM) for a single system that incorporates the \emph{pseudo-states (effects)} (they satisfy all the properties of quantum states and effects except having negative eigenvalues), and yields valid probability.

items.title: Coefficient-Range Mitigation on an 8-Bit Coherent Ising Machine
items.summary: Mapping optimization problems to the restricted coefficient range of an 8-bit CIM can distort their encoded energy landscapes. We investigate whether three coefficient-range mitigation techniques previously studied for quantum annealing---interaction extension, bounded-coefficient encoding, and augmented Lagrangian penalties---improve end-to-end optimization outcomes.

items.title: Real-Time Cryo-CMOS Photon-Number Readout from a Single SNSPD
items.summary: Measurements leveraging the intrinsic photon-number resolution of Superconducting Nanostrip Single-Photon Detectors (SNSPDs) have recently gained traction due to the simplicity of the detector design. Intrinsic photon-number measurement schemes using SNSPDs encode the photon-number information in picosecond signal timing; these systems thus require high bandwidth readout and sensitive electrical measurement equipment.

items.title: A Path Integral Method with Far-Field Expansion for Open Quantum Dynamics
items.summary: We establish a connection between the quasi-adiabatic propagator path integral (QuAPI) method and fast resummation of Dyson series (FRODS). Building on this connection, we introduce a path integral method with far-field expansion (PIFFE) for quantum systems coupled linearly to a thermal Gaussian bath.

items.title: Minimal input dimension for superactivation of one-shot zero-error quantum capacity
items.summary: The one-shot zero-error quantum capacity $\overline{Q}_0$ is studied within the framework of noncommutative graphs of quantum channels. The additivity of $\overline{Q}_0$ is proved for an arbitrary finite collection of channels with two-dimensional input spaces.

items.title: Quantum Advantage in Privacy-Preserving Hypothesis Testing via Entanglement-Assisted Classical Communication
items.summary: Quantum mechanisms satisfying quantum local differential privacy (QLDP) have been shown to achieve a quantum advantage over classical local differential privacy (LDP) mechanisms in certain hypothesis-testing problems. While previous demonstrations have considered the transmission of quantum states from users to a server, we investigate whether this advantage can persist under entanglement-assisted classical communication (EACC), where users and the server share entanglement in advance and communicate only…

items.title: Unified preparation of exact and asymptotic quantum many-body scars from Dicke states
items.summary: We propose a unified quantum algorithm for preparing exact and asymptotic quantum many-body scar (QMBS) states in the spin-1 {\it XY}, domain-wall-conserving, and Onsager scar models. Model-dependent isometries map the exact scar states to Dicke states and the target asymptotic QMBS states to gapless magnon excitations of the spin-1/2 ferromagnetic Heisenberg chain.

items.title: Coherent quantum-circuit simulation of Mueller dipole branching at small $x$: multiplicity fluctuations and DIS phenomenology
items.summary: Mueller dipole branching at small $x$ is a stochastic process in which splitting rates depend on transverse geometry. We construct a coherent quantum circuit for a regulated finite-state version of this process.

items.title: Gaussian Is All You Need: Renyi Optimizers and Optical Channel Simulation
items.summary: Preparing an entangled state faithfully requires an amount of resource given by its entanglement cost. With less entanglement, the best achievable fidelity is governed by the Rényi entanglement of formation of orders above one.

items.title: Empirical De-Quantization and Norm-Controlled Spectral Audit of Quantum Cognition Machine Learning in an Emerging Equity Market
items.summary: Quantum-inspired machine learning in econophysics describes states of financial markets through matrix Hamiltonians, using ground-state expectations to predict returns and spectral gaps to identify crises. Although early work reports encouraging advances, it remains unclear whether these stem from genuine noncommutative quantum geometry or from conventional classical regularization and scale effects.

items.title: Phonon-Aware Electron-to-Nuclear Spin Quantum Memory in NV Centers
items.summary: Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond are a promising solid-state platform for quantum memory: the electron spin can be optically initialized and read out, while nearby nuclear spins have long coherence times and can serve as storage qubits. In this work, we develop a phonon-aware open quantum system model for electron-to-nuclear spin state transfer in a single NV center.

items.title: Decoherent Histories from Local Spectral Dephasing in Quantum Many-Body Systems
items.summary: We study local spectral dephasing as a mechanism for decoherent histories in isolated quantum many-body systems. We prove that vanishing projector-weighted spectral concentration is asymptotically equivalent to vanishing time-averaged local memory.

items.title: TyxonQ: A Workflow Layer for Quantum Computing in Chemistry
items.summary: Quantum computational chemistry is often framed around a hybrid quantum solver. In practical applications, however, bottlenecks to adoption also lie in the surrounding multiscale workflow.

items.title: How Many Autonomous Encoded Qubits Force an Isotropic Noise Response?
items.summary: Depolarizing noise scales trace distances by a common factor. An encoded qubit is autonomous if its reduced input state determines its output. For $D=2^n\ge4$, autonomy forces this isotropy at a sharp threshold of $(D^2+5)/3$ generic encodings, two more than state tomography requires.

items.title: Reproducible distributions of energy-relaxation times in superconducting qubits from broadband SWAP spectroscopy
items.summary: The distribution of the qubit energy-relaxation time (T1) in a superconducting quantum processor affects its logical error rates. However, reports on qubit fabrication quality focus on the median or best-case T1 from measurements that are not reproducible due to resonant coupling to two-level system (TLS) defects whose frequencies fluctuate in time.

items.title: Efficient Quantum Algorithm for the Generalised Geography Game
items.summary: The Generalized Geography Game ($GGG$) is a two-player combinatorial game played on a directed graph, where players alternately move a token along edges without revisiting previously visited vertices. In the existing literature, determining whether an arbitrary position in a graph is a winning position for either player is a well-known $PSPACE$-complete decision problem.

items.title: A bright source of high-dimensional spatially entangled photon pairs based on beam-like Type-II SPDC
items.summary: Bright sources of high-dimensional spatially entangled photon pairs are increasingly required for the rapid advancement of quantum technologies. However, simultaneously achieving high brightness and high-dimensional spatial entanglement through spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) remains challenging.

items.title: QPAT: A Universal Quantum Machine Learning Framework for Quantum-Assisted Training and Classical Inference
items.summary: Deep learning models often struggle with sharp local optima and overfitting in limited-data regimes, and exhibit limited capacity for capturing high-order, complex probability distributions. Quantum Machine Learning (QML) models, by operating in exponentially large Hilbert spaces, can efficiently represent such distributions and provide favorable inductive biases for learning, offering a promising pathway to overcome these limitations.

items.title: Structure theorem for quantum limit cycle attractors: A geometric path-integral approach
items.summary: We show a Structure Theorem for an arbitrary separable quantum system (\(\dim\mathcal{H}\leq\aleph_0\)) that is coupled, through a symmetric bidirectional phase interface, to a self-sustaining phase-oscillator environment. Under the assumptions of \(U(1)\) covariance, instantaneous Lindblad bounded positivity, and the existence of an entrainable periodic attractor, the reduced generator is forced into a universal operator structure consisting of a state-dependent coherent recoil together with single-quantum…

items.title: Late-time OTOCs in Toda conformal field theory
items.summary: We study late-time out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs) of semi-degenerate primary fields in two-dimensional $A_{N-1}$ Toda conformal field theory. In Liouville theory ($N=2$), we find that the OTOC decays as $t^{-3/2}$ when the continuum edge dominates, correcting a previously reported constant limit.

items.title: Improved Quantum Algorithms for TSP and More
items.summary: The traveling salesman problem (TSP) is a canonical NP-hard optimization problem. For general edge weights, the classical dynamic programs of Bellman and of Held and Karp solve TSP on $n$ cities in $O^*(2^n)$ time.

items.title: When Malus' Law Meets the Wigner-Bell Inequality: Violation by Nonseparable Classical Light
items.summary: Bell-type inequalities are commonly associated with quantum nonlocality, yet their mathematical structure also reflects more general constraints on the joint probability distributions assigned to measurements performed in different contexts. Here we examine this distinction through the Wigner--Bell inequality using a classical optical field with two nonseparable degrees of freedom.

items.title: Superconductivity from the Berry connection from many-electron wave functions: $U(1)$ gauge fluctuation, gauge invariance, and superconductivity
items.summary: The electromagnetic $U(1)$ gauge invariance and superconductivity are examined by employing the Berry connection from many-electron wave functions and the fluctuations of it that give rise to the probabilistic random transitions among quantum states. The gauge invariance in the classical electrodynamics is regarded as the requirement that extracts unaffected parts by the gauge fluctuation.

items.title: On-Demand Tailoring of High-Dimensional Orbital Angular Momentum States via a Phase-Only Hologram
items.summary: Photonic orbital angular momentum (OAM) provides a naturally discrete and unbounded Hilbert space for high-dimensional encoding and has emerged as a powerful degree of freedom for advanced information processing. On-demand tailoring of both the amplitude and phase profiles of high-dimensional OAM states is essential for numerous applications, particularly in quantum information science.

items.title: Dimensional crossover to a slow disordered spin bath below the mean spin spacing
items.summary: How thin must a layer of spins be to act as a two-dimensional bath? For nitrogen spins around an NV$^-$ centre in diamond, a cluster expansion with flip-flopping outer spins gives a crossover near the mean spin spacing.

items.title: Amatlas: A 2D Array Architecture for Union-Find Decoding Without Global Coordination
items.summary: Real-time decoding of the surface code is essential for fault-tolerant quantum computing, and scaling the decoder to large code distances in hardware remains a challenge. The locality of Union-Find (UF) decoding makes it a leading candidate for such a decoder in distributed hardware.

items.title: High-Dimensional Single-Photon Frequency Conversion for Orbital Angular Momentum Comb State
items.summary: The orbital angular momentum (OAM) degree of freedom provides an important resource for constructing high-dimensional optical quantum information systems. However, the generation of high-dimensional single-photon OAM comb state and its high-fidelity frequency conversion remain challenging due to limited spatial modulation resolution, imperfect mode matching, and finite nonlinear conversion efficiency.

items.title: A scalable dense silicon qubit architecture with logical operations
items.summary: Fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC) requires a large number of physical qubits to encode logical qubits with sufficiently low error rates. Silicon spin qubits are a promising platform because of their small footprint, compatibility with semiconductor manufacturing technologies, and demonstrated high-fidelity operations.

items.title: Noetics, a New but Old Understanding of Mind and Reality
items.summary: Noetics is examined here as an interdisciplinary approach to how lived experience becomes a knowledge claim and informs action. This narrative review brings historical philosophy into dialogue with cognitive science, contemporary theories of consciousness, contemplative traditions, and artificial intelligence.
items.source: Journal of Advanced Research in Social Sciences

items.title: Early visual experience contributes to the calibration of higher-order body representations
items.summary: Higher-order body representations, including representations of body shape and size, play an important role in maintaining perceptual constancy in touch. However, whether the development of these representations depends on early visual experience remains unclear.

items.title: Conversing with a Conversational Agent: A Real Conversation, Not a Simulated One
items.summary: The claim that interactions with artificial conversational agents merely simulate human conversation rests on a philosophical distinction between reproducing the observable features of an activity and actually performing it. Although this distinction is appropriate for certain physical phenomena, its application to linguistic and symbolic activities is far less straightforward.

items.title: Toward a Composite Framework of Consciousness: Integrating Brain–Body Interactions, Sentience, and Neuroimaging in Disorders of Consciousness
items.summary: The accurate assessment of consciousness in non-communicative patients remains a major challenge for neuroscience and clinical care. While behavioral scales such as the Coma Recovery Scale–Revised (CRS-R) provide standardized tools for diagnosis, they are limited by patients’ motor impairments and the absence of subjective report.

items.summary: We introduce a chromatically constrained tensor-product construction that generates sparse recurrent computational graphs whose coloring bounds the number of sequential execution phases: vertices are computational units, edges are causal message-passing channels, and the graph can grow arbitrarily large while its chromatic causal depth stays fixed. items.title: Universal quantum gate set for multimode Schrödinger cat states stabilized by nonlocal dissipation engineering
items.summary: Schr\"odinger cat states provide a hardware-efficient platform for bosonic quantum error correction by encoding logical information in protected manifolds of harmonic oscillators. While previous work has demonstrated the dissipative stabilization of multimode Schr\"odinger cat states as robust quantum memories, a framework for universal quantum computation has remained unavailable.

items.title: Quantum Annealing Complexity and Stochastic Quantum Control
items.summary: This thesis investigates two central challenges for quantum computing: identifying when quantum annealing can offer a computational advantage, and developing effective methods to control realistic quantum systems. It establishes complexity bounds for an adiabatic algorithm for combinatorial optimization, showing a universal quadratic advantage while highlighting the practical difficulty of realizing the required schedule.

items.title: Fixed-preparation short-time reconstruction of class-D BdG endpoint masses
items.summary: In one-dimensional class-D superconductors, the relative signs of the Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) masses at particle-hole-invariant momenta fix the bulkinvariant. Band energies and transition-frequency peak locations alone cannot determine these signs.

items.title: The waggle dance in honeybees: a language - beyond metaphor
items.summary: The waggle dance reports an outbound flight vector with a ritualized whole-body movement to a location in the environment surrounding the bee colony. This informative gesture is embedded in the cognitive faculties involved in organizing the social life inside and outside the hive during foraging for food and finding a new nest site.

items.title: Actualization and the Quantum Mechanical Universe: Dissolving the Gap
items.summary: The actualization gap—the apparent discontinuity between the classical probability distribution delivered by decoherence and the single definite outcome that appears in experience—has been treated in the foundations literature as an outstanding problem in the physics of quantum measurement. This paper argues that the gap is not a physical problem and admits no physical solution.

items.title: Does Total Knowledge Mute Emotion? A Thought Experiment using Large Language Models
items.summary: This paper examines whether comprehensive knowledge acquisition attenuates emotional experience through a thought experiment that uses large language models (LLMs). We propose that LLMs, which possess extensive propositional knowledge yet lack phenomenal consciousness, serve as philosophical instruments for isolating the knowledge variable from other cognitive attributes.

items.title: Virtual reality as a neural state-modulating technology: EEG complexity during VR gameplay versus VR gameplay viewing
items.summary: Pharmacological agents and brain stimulation can modulate conscious states, but offer limited control over the structure of the experience itself. Virtual reality (VR) can alter subjective experience while allowing its structure to be experimentally controlled.

items.title: Effects of auditory sensory stimulation on consciousness and physiological parameters among individuals with disorders of consciousness: a systematic review and meta-analysis
items.summary: Objective: To systematically evaluate the effects of auditory sensory stimulation (SS) on consciousness levels and physiological parameters in patients with disorders of consciousness (DOC). Furthermore, this study aimed to explore intervention characteristics based on the frequency, intensity, time, and type (FITT) framework that may influence treatment effects and to investigate potential sources of between-study heterogeneity.

items.title: Nāgārjunian Madhyamaka and relational quantum mechanics: the limits of relational foundationalism
items.summary: Comparisons between Mahāyāna Buddhism and quantum physics often equate emptiness with indeterminacy, dependent arising with quantum relationality and entanglement with universal interconnection. Such equations conflate four levels: experimental results, mathematical formalism, interpretations of quantum theory and metaphysical extrapolations.

items.title: Genuinely Quantum Algorithms for Bio-inspired Meta-heuristic Optimization
items.summary: Quantum computation offers a promising pathway toward advancing meta-heuristic optimization, particularly in Nature-inspired paradigms such as genetic algorithms and swarm intelligence. This study conducts a systematic literature review of fifteen major meta-heuristics to assess current efforts toward their quantum realization.

Setting down what our programs have learned so that others can use it, contest it, and test it, we work through the central tensions that every QISE graduate program must negotiate: between depth in a home discipline and breadth across the field, between structured…

items.title: Opposite post-processing orders of fermionic horizon channels and their quantum-resource monotonicity
items.summary: Studies of relativistic quantum information in noninertial and black-hole settings often focus on specific input states and resource functionals, leaving the common origin of recurring monotonic trends in quantum resources and correlations unclear. In this work, we identify a common channel-ordering structure from the complementary exterior and interior reductions of the effective single-mode fermionic horizon transformation, representing the physically accessible and inaccessible sectors, respectively.

items.title: Causality, determinism and predictability: Probing nature through classical and quantum eyes
items.summary: In this article, mainly focussed on students and interested readers, we discuss how the understanding of causality, determinism and predictability is transformed as we move from the classical world view to the quantum description. We first explain how determinism and predictability operate in classical dynamics and outline the notion of causality.

items.summary: This paper presents a panoramic sight of philosophical and methodological problems concerning interdisciplinary interaction of philosophy and cognitive sciences in the context of reflections upon Natalia Smirnova’s book “Imagination, Language, Creativity. Philosophy and Cognitive Sciences in the Study of Creative Activity of Consciousness” (Moscow, Saint Petersburg: Tsentr gumanitarnykh initsiativ, 2025).

items.title: Parameter-shift rules for gradients in boson sampling experiments
items.summary: Using a robust photon loss model for photonic quantum experiments, we derive n th order parameter-shift rules (PSRs) for computing gradients of Fock boson sampling transition probabilities where n photons are sent into a lossy interferometer. We also show that one cannot naturally generalize this gradient recipe to the case of Gaussian boson sampling.

items.title: Quantum Graph Neural Networks: Architectures, Trainability, and Applications
items.summary: Quantum graph neural networks (QGNNs) apply parametrized quantum circuits to graph-structured data, with the aim of overcoming limits of classical graph neural networks in scalability, expressivity, and long-range information flow. Since the first Hamiltonian-based model in 2019, the field has produced many architectures, applications, and claims, but the evidence behind them has not been assessed systematically.

items.title: Almost-quantum correlations violate information causality
items.summary: Information causality (IC), a generalization of the no-signalling principle, states that communicating m classical bits cannot give the receiver access to more than m bits of information about the sender's independent data. Although IC holds in quantum theory and excludes a broad class of supra-quantum correlations, its validity for the almost-quantum set has remained open.

items.title: Ontology-constrained multi-LLM scoring of hypothesis support in the predictive processing literature
items.summary: Fragmentation is common in interdisciplinary fields with diverse methods and theoretical commitments. Predictive coding neuroscience is a clear example: its literature spans computational theory, electrophysiology, imaging, behavior, and modeling, creating a synthesis problem that conventional meta-analysis cannot easily resolve.

items.summary: Every data science pipeline begins with a measurement. When that measurement is made by a quantum mechanical system—exploiting superposition, entanglement, and coherence—the sensor can in principle surpass the classical shot-noise precision limit.

items.title: Indivisible Stochastic Processes and the Quantum Formalism: An Interpretive Synthesis around Barandes's Correspondence
items.summary: Quantum theory remains empirically unmatched in its domain, yet its conceptual foundations—measurement, the status of the wavefunction, and the classical limit—remain contested. A research programme due to Barandes reframes unitary quantum mechanics in terms of indivisible (non-Markovian) stochastic processes on configuration space, with unistochastic transition matrices supplying the bridge to complex amplitudes.

items.title: Exploring Discrete Algorithms in Quantum Computing
items.summary: Quantum computing introduces a new computational paradigm by extending the classical binary representation of information through quantum bits, which can exist in superposed states and exhibit entanglement. This work presents a systematic study of fundamental concepts, computational mechanisms, and discrete algorithms in quantum computing.

items.title: Navigating Quantum Education at the University level: Pedagogical Pathways and a Roadmap for Textbook Selection
items.summary: Instruction in quantum mechanics (QM) is often categorized by its entry point as 'wave-first' or 'spin-first', yet these labels lack consistent definitions and overlook other established or emerging approaches. Moreover, while capturing broad differences in topic selection and sequencing, this binary framing obscures critical differences in contextualization--how three dimensions (mathematical tools, phenomena and experiments, and theoretical concepts) are framed and connected to support student sensemaking.

items.title: Quantum Random Number Generators: principles, practical challenges and mainstream implementations
items.summary: Quantum random number generators have become a cornerstone technology for modern digital cryptography, including key generation, quantum key distribution, and post-quantum cryptographic systems. While existing reviews typically concentrate on specific entropy sources or implementation platforms, a comprehensive perspective encompassing the complete QRNG pipeline remains largely absent.

items.title: Liquid Integrated Network as Candidate Substrate for Artificial Consciousness
items.summary: Whether artificial intelligence (AI) system allows for generating machine consciousness has been a “grand challenge” which however must be answered in this day and age. Most contemporary AI is implemented on large scale solid-state electronic hardware, whereas biological consciousness is supported by much smaller sized space within a fluid-rich brain.

items.title: A Reflexive Psychophysical Universe
items.summary: This paper develops reflexive monism (RM), a panentheist, psychophysical, dual-aspect monist form of cosmopsychism, as a framework for understanding how consciousness relates to energy/matter in both the ground of being and the manifest world. I begin by distinguishing “mind”, largely constituted by unconscious information processing in contemporary cognitive science, from “consciousness”, understood as phenomenal experience.

items.title: Endogenous suspension of phenomenal consciousness during extended cessation: Regional homogeneity analysis of multi-participant 7T fMRI of an advanced meditative endpoint
items.summary: Extended cessation (EC) is a rare advanced meditative state characterized by the voluntary absence of reportable phenomenal experience, followed by reproducible aftereffects including immense mental clarity, equanimity, and peace. EC offers an endogenous model for investigating the mechanisms of consciousness.

items.title: When lies look like noise: certifying untrusted entanglement swapping
items.summary: Entanglement swapping lets quantum repeaters distribute entanglement over long distances, a prerequisite for the quantum internet. We study its security in a noisy network whose intermediate nodes perform the quantum operations faithfully but may misreport the classical outcome that end users rely on.

items.title: Analog Explorations of Quantum State Measurement
items.summary: The awkward disconnect in the postulates of quantum mechanics between the continuous, deterministic, linear, and unitary evolution governed by Schrödinger's equation and the discontinuous, stochastic, nonlinear, and nonunitary measurement process has vexed physicists for decades. Intuition from classical mechanics, statistical mechanics, and dynamical systems theory suggests that such a process might be modeled with a nonlinear system of differential equations.

items.title: SynDebug: A Framework to Debug Logic Bugs in Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing Programs
items.summary: Fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC) introduces substantial systems-level complexity through quantum error correction (QEC), making debugging FTQC programs challenging. Existing quantum debugging approaches primarily target logical-level circuits and do not naturally support debugging within realistic FTQC execution flows.

items.summary: The central claim of this thesis is simple but underappreciated: the primary bottleneck in near-term quantum computing is not a shortage of algorithms; it is a lack of systematic decision-making. Which problem instances should we test?

items.title: The entangled loop: Emotion, interference and hierarchy in the architecture of consciousness
items.summary: Why does consciousness feel like something, and why is experience unified rather than fragmented? We propose that these properties arise from an entangled trefoil of emotion, interference-based inference and hierarchical orchestration, shaped by the thermodynamic constraint that living systems must remain far from equilibrium using limited energy.
